question: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is a:
solution_text:
The correct answer is single-member body.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is a single-member (independent) constitutional authority, established under Article 148 of the Constitution of India. (भारत के नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक — एकल सदस्यीय निकाय)

 

• The CAG is appointed by the President of India and holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

 

• The CAG is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and audits all receipts and expenditure of the Government of India and state governments, including bodies substantially financed by government.

 

• The CAG can only be removed from office in a manner similar to a Supreme Court judge, i.e., by a presidential order after an address by both Houses of Parliament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CAG submits three types of audit reports to the President — relating to appropriation accounts, finance accounts, and public undertakings — which are then laid before Parliament.

 

• The office of CAG is often called the guardian of the public purse, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called it the most important officer under the Constitution of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Two-member body (Option 1): Incorrect — the CAG is not a multi-member body.

 

• Three-member body (Option 2): Incorrect — this describes bodies such as some other commissions, not the CAG.

 

• Six-member body (Option 4): Incorrect — there is no such provision for the CAG; it is a single, independent constitutional office.

question: Which of the following led English company in Battle of Plassey (1757)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Clive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah. (प्लासी का युद्ध — रॉबर्ट क्लाइव)

 

• The battle was won by the British largely due to the betrayal of Mir Jafar, the Nawab's commander-in-chief, who did not commit his troops to the fight.

 

• The victory at Plassey laid the foundation of British political power in India and led to the installation of Mir Jafar as the puppet Nawab of Bengal.

 

• This battle is regarded as one of the most decisive battles in Indian history, marking the beginning of British colonial rule in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Battle of Buxar (1764) further consolidated British control, after which the Company acquired Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha in 1765.

 

• Robert Clive later became the first British Governor of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 1): Governor-General of India (1848–1856), known for the Doctrine of Lapse; not associated with Plassey.

 

• Captain Hodson (Option 2): A British military officer associated with the capture of Bahadur Shah Zafar during the Revolt of 1857.

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 3): The first Governor-General of Bengal (1773–1785), not connected with the Battle of Plassey.

question: As the river enters the plain it twists and turns forming large bends known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is meanders.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As a river enters a plain, its velocity decreases, and it develops large, sweeping loops or bends called meanders. (नदी का मोड़ — मिएंडर)

 

• Meanders form due to the interplay of erosion on the outer (concave) bank and deposition on the inner (convex) bank of the river curve.

 

• Continued meandering can eventually cut off a loop from the main channel, forming an ox-bow lake.

 

• This is a characteristic feature of rivers in their mature/old stage, typically seen in floodplains such as those of the Ganga and Brahmaputra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Levees are raised river banks formed by repeated deposition of sediments during floods.

 

• Floodplains are flat areas along a river formed by sediment deposition during periodic flooding.

 

NOTE

 

• Ox-bow (Option 1): This is the lake formed when a meander gets cut off, not the twisting/turning of the river itself.

 

• Levees (Option 2): These are raised embankments formed by flood deposits, not bends in the river course.

 

• Floodplains (Option 3): These are the flat, low-lying areas adjacent to a river, not the term for the river's bends.

question: What does the letter ‘M’ stand for in the MRTP Act 1969?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monopolies.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act, 1969 was enacted to prevent the concentration of economic power and curb monopolistic and restrictive trade practices. (एकाधिकार और प्रतिबंधात्मक व्यापार व्यवहार अधिनियम — मोनोपोलीज़)

 

• The Act established the MRTP Commission to investigate and regulate unfair and restrictive trade practices in India.

 

• The MRTP Act was a product of India's pre-liberalisation, License Raj-era regulatory framework.

 

• The Act was eventually repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, which established the Competition Commission of India (CCI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Competition Act, 2002 shifted the regulatory focus from curbing monopolies to promoting fair competition in Indian markets.

 

• The CCI became fully functional in 2009, replacing the erstwhile MRTP Commission.

 

NOTE

 

• Monopolistic (Option 1): Not the correct expansion — the Act's title uses the noun 'Monopolies', not the adjective 'Monopolistic'.

 

• Multi (Option 3): Not related to the MRTP Act's title in any way.

 

• Monopoly (Option 4): Incorrect — the Act's title uses the plural form 'Monopolies', not the singular 'Monopoly'.

question: Harihara and Bukka established an independent state in Karnataka and established the capital city Vijayanagar on the banks of river _____________ in 1336.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tungabhadra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, two brothers who founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE. (विजयनगर साम्राज्य — तुंगभद्रा नदी)

 

• They established their capital city, Vijayanagara ('City of Victory'), on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra River in present-day Karnataka.

 

• The empire was founded partly under the guidance of the saint Vidyaranya and went on to become one of the greatest Hindu empires of medieval South India.

 

• The ruins of Vijayanagara are located at Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire reached its zenith under Krishnadeva Raya of the Tuluva dynasty (1509–1529).

 

• The empire finally declined after its defeat in the Battle of Talikota (1565) against the combined Deccan Sultanates.

 

NOTE

 

• Betwa (Option 1): A tributary of the Yamuna, flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; unrelated to Vijayanagara.

 

• Mahanadi (Option 3): A major river of Chhattisgarh and Odisha, not connected to the founding of Vijayanagara.

 

• Tapi (Option 4): A west-flowing river of central India, draining into the Arabian Sea near Surat; not linked to Vijayanagara.

question:
Match the industrial plant with its location.

Name of Industrial Plant | Related Location

1. BALCO | A) Burnpur

2. IISCO | B) Chennai

3. NFL | C) Korba

4. ICF | D) Bhatinda
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-C,2-A,3-D,4-B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BALCO (Bharat Aluminium Company) is located at Korba, Chhattisgarh, matching 1-C. (भारत एल्युमिनियम कंपनी — कोरबा)

 

• IISCO (Indian Iron and Steel Company) has its steel plant at Burnpur, West Bengal (in the Asansol industrial belt), matching 2-A.

 

• NFL (National Fertilizers Limited) operates a plant at Bhatinda, Punjab, matching 3-D.

 

• ICF (Integral Coach Factory), which manufactures railway coaches, is located at Perambur, Chennai, matching 4-B.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• BALCO is one of India's leading aluminium producers and was originally a PSU, later divested to the Vedanta Group.

 

• ICF Chennai, established in 1955, is one of the largest rail coach manufacturing units in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (1-A,2-B,3-C,4-D): Incorrect — none of these plant-location pairs match the correct locations.

 

• Option 2 (1-C,2-A,3-B,4-D): Incorrect — while BALCO-Korba and IISCO-Burnpur are correctly matched here, NFL and ICF are wrongly matched.

 

• Option 4 (1-D,2-A,3-B,4-C): Incorrect — BALCO is wrongly matched to Bhatinda instead of Korba, and the remaining pairs are also incorrect.

question: Identify the correct chemical formula of chloroform.
solution_text:
The correct answer is CHCl3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chloroform, chemically known as trichloromethane, has the molecular formula CHCl3. (क्लोरोफॉर्म — CHCl3)

 

• It is a colourless, sweet-smelling, dense liquid that was historically used as an anaesthetic in surgery.

 

• Chloroform is also widely used as a solvent in laboratories and industry, and as a precursor in the production of refrigerants.

 

• It consists of one carbon, one hydrogen, and three chlorine atoms bonded together.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chloroform was first synthesised independently in 1831 by several chemists, including Samuel Guthrie and Eugène Soubeiran.

 

• Prolonged exposure to chloroform is now known to be toxic and carcinogenic, so it has largely been replaced by safer anaesthetics.

 

NOTE

 

• CHCl (Option 2): An incomplete/incorrect formula — carbon would have an unfilled valency and cannot exist as a stable neutral molecule.

 

• CHCl2 (Option 3): Also chemically invalid for a stable neutral compound corresponding to chloroform.

 

• CH2Cl2 (Option 4): This is the formula for dichloromethane (methylene chloride), a different compound, not chloroform.

question: How much percentage of oxygen is present in the atmosphere?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 21%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth's atmosphere is composed mainly of nitrogen (about 78%) and oxygen (about 21%), with the remaining ~1% comprising argon, carbon dioxide, and trace gases. (वायुमंडल में ऑक्सीजन — 21%)

 

• Oxygen (O2) is essential for respiration in most living organisms and for combustion processes.

 

• The composition of the atmosphere remains fairly constant up to an altitude of about 100 km (the homosphere).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nitrogen, at about 78%, is the most abundant gas in the atmosphere and is relatively inert.

 

• Argon (~0.93%) and carbon dioxide (~0.04%) make up most of the remaining atmospheric composition.

 

NOTE

 

• 39% (Option 1): Far higher than the actual proportion of oxygen in the atmosphere.

 

• 79% (Option 2): This closely matches the proportion of nitrogen, not oxygen, in the atmosphere.

 

• 10% (Option 3): Too low to be the actual atmospheric percentage of oxygen.

question: In which season is Sarhul celebrated in Jharkhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spring.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sarhul is one of the most important festivals of the tribal communities of Jharkhand (notably the Oraon, Munda and Ho tribes), celebrated in the spring season, typically in the Hindi month of Chaitra (March–April). (सरहुल पर्व — झारखंड, वसंत ऋतु)

 

• The festival marks the worship of the Sal tree and celebrates the blossoming of Sal flowers, symbolising the start of the new agricultural year.

 

• It is also known as Baha Parab among the Santhal community and involves worship of the village deity in the sacred grove.

 

• Sarhul is closely linked to nature worship and the traditional Sarna faith practised by many tribal groups of Jharkhand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major festivals of Jharkhand include Sohrai (harvest festival) and Karma, both associated with agricultural and nature worship.

 

• Jharkhand's Sarhul festival is similar in spirit to spring festivals like Vasant Panchami, celebrated elsewhere in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Autumn (Option 2): Incorrect — Sarhul is not an autumn festival; festivals like Sohrai are associated with the autumn/winter harvest season.

 

• Monsoon (Option 3): Incorrect — Sarhul precedes the monsoon and is tied to the flowering of the Sal tree in spring.

 

• Winter (Option 4): Incorrect — Sarhul is celebrated in spring (Chaitra), not winter.

question: What is the average thickness of the continental crust of earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 30 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The continental crust of the Earth has an average thickness of about 30 km, though it can range from around 25 km to over 70 km under major mountain ranges. (महाद्वीपीय क्रस्ट — औसत मोटाई 30 किमी)

 

• In contrast, the oceanic crust is much thinner, averaging only about 5–10 km.

 

• The continental crust is composed mainly of granitic (SIAL — silica and aluminium) rocks, making it lighter and thicker than the oceanic crust.

 

• The crust is the outermost solid layer of the Earth, lying above the mantle, and its thickness varies significantly with topography — thickest beneath high mountain ranges like the Himalayas.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The oceanic crust is composed mainly of denser basaltic (SIMA — silica and magnesium) rocks.

 

• The boundary between the crust and the mantle is called the Mohorovičić Discontinuity (Moho).

 

NOTE

 

• 300 km (Option 1): Far too large — this exceeds even the thickness of the entire crust-plus-upper-mantle lithosphere in most estimates.

 

• 5 km (Option 2): This roughly corresponds to the average thickness of the thinner oceanic crust, not the continental crust.

 

• 2.5 km (Option 4): Far too small to represent the average continental crust thickness.

question: Which of the following events was conducted by the Ministry of Ayush, GoI to mark the 100-day countdown to the International Day of Yoga 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yoga Mahotsav.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ministry of AYUSH, Government of India, organises 'Yoga Mahotsav' every year to mark the 100-day countdown to the International Day of Yoga (21 June). (योग महोत्सव — आयुष मंत्रालय)

 

• For International Day of Yoga 2022 (the 8th edition), the 100-day countdown event, Yoga Mahotsav, was flagged off around March 2022.

 

• The event aims to create public awareness and mass participation ahead of the International Day of Yoga, involving demonstrations of the Common Yoga Protocol.

 

• International Day of Yoga was first observed in 2015, following its adoption by the UN General Assembly in December 2014 on India's proposal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The theme for International Day of Yoga 2022 was 'Yoga for Humanity'.

 

• The Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), New Delhi, is the nodal institute of the Ministry of AYUSH for organising such yoga events.

 

NOTE

 

• Yoga Utsav (Option 2): Not the official name used by the Ministry of AYUSH for this particular 100-day countdown event.

 

• Yoga Sutra (Option 3): Refers to the classical text on yoga philosophy compiled by sage Patanjali, not an event.

 

• Yoga Umang (Option 4): Not the name of any official Ministry of AYUSH event for the International Day of Yoga countdown.

question: Who moved the Objective Resolution that was later adapted as the Preamble of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Objective Resolution was moved by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946. (उद्देश्य प्रस्ताव — जवाहरलाल नेहरू)

 

• The resolution laid down the fundamental philosophy and basic principles that later became the framework of the Preamble to the Constitution of India.

 

• It declared India to be an independent, sovereign republic and guaranteed justice, equality, and freedom to all its citizens.

 

• The Objective Resolution was unanimously adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 January 1947.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble is often described as the 'identity card' of the Constitution, and it was the last part to be finalised by the Constituent Assembly.

 

• The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, and it came into force on 26 January 1950.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajendra Prasad (Option 1): Served as the President of the Constituent Assembly, but did not move the Objective Resolution.

 

• JB Kripalani (Option 2): A senior Congress leader and Constituent Assembly member, not the mover of the Objective Resolution.

 

• BR Ambedkar (Option 4): Chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution but did not move the Objective Resolution.

question: Which of the following pairs of musicians and their instruments is INCORRECT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is K Vaidyanathan – Sitar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kunnakudi R. Vaidyanathan, popularly known as K. Vaidyanathan, was a renowned Carnatic musician famous for playing the violin, not the sitar — making this pairing incorrect. (कुन्नाकुडी वैद्यनाथन — वायलिन वादक)

 

• The question asks for the INCORRECT pairing, and 'K Vaidyanathan – Sitar' misrepresents his actual instrument.

 

• The other three pairs given in the question are all factually correct associations of well-known Indian classical musicians with their instruments.

 

• Ustad Vilayat Khan was one of the greatest sitar players of the 20th century, founder of the Imdadkhani gharana style of sitar playing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pt. Ram Narayan popularised the sarangi as a solo classical instrument, elevating it from its earlier role as a mere accompanying instrument.

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan was a legendary shehnai player and the first classical musician to be awarded the Bharat Ratna, in 2001.

 

NOTE

 

• Pt. Ram Narayan – Sarangi (Option 2): This is a correct pairing, so it is not the answer.

 

• Ustad Vilayat Khan – Sitar (Option 3): This is a correct pairing, so it is not the answer.

 

• Bismillah Khan – Shehnai (Option 4): This is a correct pairing, so it is not the answer.

question: Which of the following becomes the first district in India to cover 100% households under ABPMJAY- SEHAT scheme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samba, Jammu and Kashmir.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Samba district in Jammu and Kashmir became the first district in India to achieve 100% household coverage (Golden Card registration) under the Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY SEHAT scheme in 2022. (साम्बा जिला — जम्मू और कश्मीर, आयुष्मान भारत)

 

• The SEHAT (Social, Endeavour for Health and Telemedicine) scheme extends the Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY health insurance cover to all residents of Jammu and Kashmir, unlike the income-based criteria used elsewhere in India.

 

• Under SEHAT, every resident of J&K is entitled to a health insurance cover of ₹5 lakh per family per year, similar to PM-JAY.

 

• This achievement in Samba was highlighted as a major milestone in universal health coverage under the scheme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, launched nationally in 2018, is the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme.

 

• The SEHAT scheme for Jammu & Kashmir was launched on 26 December 2020, on the birth anniversary of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

 

NOTE

 

• Pratapgarh, Rajasthan (Option 2): Not the first district to achieve 100% coverage under this specific J&K-focused scheme.

 

• Kheda, Gujarat (Option 3): Not associated with this particular ABPMJAY-SEHAT milestone.

 

• Mansa, Punjab (Option 4): Not associated with this particular ABPMJAY-SEHAT milestone.

question: In India census is held regularly every ______ year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Census of India is conducted regularly every 10 years (decennially), under the provisions of the Census Act, 1948. (भारत की जनगणना — प्रति 10 वर्ष)

 

• The first synchronous census of India was conducted in 1881, and censuses have been held every 10 years since then without a break.

 

• The most recent census was conducted in 2011; the 2021 census was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

 

• The census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2011 Census was the 15th Census of India and the 7th after independence, recording a population of over 121 crore.

 

• Census data is used extensively for delimitation of constituencies, planning, and resource allocation.

 

NOTE

 

• 8th (Option 1): Incorrect — the census interval is not 8 years.

 

• 12th (Option 3): Incorrect — the census interval is not 12 years.

 

• 5th (Option 4): Incorrect — the census interval is not 5 years.

question: Who among the following launched the Scheme “SHRESHTA” for residential education for students in High school in Targeted Areas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Virendra Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The SHRESHTA (Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas) was launched by Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment. (श्रेष्ठ योजना — वीरेंद्र कुमार)

 

• SHRESHTA aims to provide quality residential education to meritorious Scheduled Caste (SC) students from Class 9 and 11 in top private/government residential schools.

 

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, targeting SC-dominated and aspirational districts.

 

• Admission under SHRESHTA is done through a national entrance test conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• SHRESHTA is one of several schemes under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at the socio-economic upliftment of SC students, alongside schemes like PM-AJAY.

 

• The scheme was formally launched in 2021, and complements existing schemes for Scheduled Tribe (Eklavya Model Residential Schools) students.

 

NOTE

 

• Piyush Goel (Option 2): Refers to Union Minister Piyush Goyal, whose portfolios include Commerce and Industry, not the SHRESHTA scheme.

 

• Vijay Goel (Option 3): A BJP leader and former Union Minister, not associated with launching the SHRESHTA scheme.

 

• P P Chaudhary (Option 4): A BJP Member of Parliament, not associated with launching the SHRESHTA scheme.

question: Which of the following dance forms is associated with the state of Arunachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buiya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Buiya is a traditional folk dance of the Digaru Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh. (बुइया नृत्य — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It is typically performed during festivals and social occasions, often accompanied by traditional musical instruments and colourful tribal attire.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh is home to numerous tribal communities, each with distinct dance forms reflecting their unique cultural heritage.

 

• Other important folk dances of Arunachal Pradesh include Popir (Adi tribe) and Aji Lamu (Monpa tribe).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Monpa tribe's Mask Dance is performed during Buddhist festivals like Losar in Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• Garba (Option 4), in contrast, is a well-known folk dance of Gujarat, performed during Navratri.

 

NOTE

 

• Panwariya (Option 1): A folk dance associated with regions like Uttar Pradesh, not Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• Dhaman (Option 2): Not a recognised folk dance of Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• Garba (Option 4): A famous folk dance of Gujarat, unrelated to Arunachal Pradesh.

question: The Commonwealth Games 2018 were held at which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gold coast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2018 Commonwealth Games (XXI Commonwealth Games) were held at Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia, from 4 to 15 April 2018. (राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2018 — गोल्ड कोस्ट, ऑस्ट्रेलिया)

 

• India finished third in the medal tally at the 2018 Commonwealth Games, with 66 medals (26 gold, 20 silver, 20 bronze).

 

• This was the fifth time Australia hosted the Commonwealth Games, more than any other nation.

 

• The 2018 Games notably had more women's events than men's events for the first time in Commonwealth Games history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The next Commonwealth Games (2022) were held in Birmingham, England.

 

• The 2026 Commonwealth Games are scheduled to be held in Glasgow, Scotland.

 

NOTE

 

• Edinburgh (Option 2): Hosted the Commonwealth Games in 1970 and 1986, not 2018.

 

• Victoria (Option 3): Refers to Victoria, Canada, which hosted the Commonwealth Games in 1994, not 2018.

 

• Kuala Lumpur (Option 4): Hosted the Commonwealth Games in 1998, not 2018.

question: Identify the organism that is NOT a pseudocoelomate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Scorpions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A pseudocoelomate is an organism with a false body cavity (pseudocoel) that is not completely lined by mesoderm; this is characteristic of the phylum Aschelminthes (Nematoda). (कूट-प्रगुहा — नेमाटोड)

 

• Ancylostoma (hookworm), Ascaris (roundworm), and Wuchereria (filarial worm) are all nematodes (roundworms) and are classic examples of pseudocoelomate animals.

 

• Scorpions, on the other hand, belong to the phylum Arthropoda, class Arachnida, and possess a true coelom (haemocoel), not a pseudocoel.

 

• This makes Scorpions the odd one out among the four given organisms with respect to body cavity type.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other examples of pseudocoelomates include Rotifers and Trichinella.

 

• True coelomate animals include phyla such as Annelida, Mollusca, Arthropoda, Echinodermata, and Chordata.

 

NOTE

 

• Ancylostoma (Option 1): A nematode (hookworm) and hence a pseudocoelomate, so it is not the answer.

 

• Ascaris (Option 2): A nematode (roundworm) and hence a pseudocoelomate, so it is not the answer.

 

• Wuchereria (Option 3): A nematode (filarial worm) and hence a pseudocoelomate, so it is not the answer.

question:
Plan revenue expenditure relates to _______.

I. Five-year plans

II. Salaries and pensions
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plan revenue expenditure refers to the revenue expenditure incurred on Central Plan schemes and Central assistance for State and Union Territory Plans, i.e., expenditure tied to the Five-Year Plans. (योजना राजस्व व्यय — पंचवर्षीय योजनाएं)

 

• Statement I is correct: Plan revenue expenditure directly relates to spending on schemes under the Five-Year Plans.

 

• Statement II is incorrect: Salaries and pensions of existing government establishments are treated as Non-Plan revenue expenditure, being recurring, committed expenditure not tied to new plan schemes.

 

• This Plan/Non-Plan classification of government expenditure was used in India's budgeting until it was discontinued from the 2017–18 Budget onward, replaced by the revenue/capital expenditure classification.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Non-Plan expenditure traditionally covered items like interest payments, defence expenditure, subsidies, salaries, and pensions.

 

• The distinction between Plan and Non-Plan expenditure was replaced by the Revenue and Capital expenditure classification starting Budget 2017-18, on the recommendation of a committee led by Sudhir Mankad.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 2): Incorrect, since Statement I is factually correct.

 

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect, since Statement II (salaries and pensions) falls under Non-Plan, not Plan, revenue expenditure.

 

• Only II (Option 4): Incorrect, since salaries and pensions are Non-Plan expenditure, while Plan revenue expenditure relates to Five-Year Plans (Statement I).

question: The word Manuscripts derived from which of the following language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Latin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word 'manuscript' is derived from the Latin words 'manu' (hand) and 'scriptus' (written), together meaning 'written by hand'. (हस्तलिपि — लैटिन भाषा)

 

• A manuscript refers to any document, text, or composition written by hand, as opposed to being printed or mechanically reproduced.

 

• In historical and archival study, manuscripts are important primary sources for understanding ancient literature, religion, and administration.

 

• India has a rich tradition of manuscripts written on materials like palm leaf (tadpatra) and birch bark (bhojpatra).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Mission for Manuscripts (NAMAMI) was launched by the Government of India in 2003 to survey, document, and preserve India's manuscript heritage.

 

• India is estimated to hold one of the largest collections of manuscripts in the world, numbering in the several millions.

 

NOTE

 

• Prakrit (Option 2): An ancient Indian vernacular language group, not the source of the word 'manuscript'.

 

• Sanskrit (Option 3): A classical Indian language in which many manuscripts are written, but not the etymological source of the English word 'manuscript'.

 

• Greek (Option 4): Not the language from which the word 'manuscript' is derived.

question: The Appropriation bill, 2022 was passed in Lok Sabha on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is May 10, 2022.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Appropriation Bill gives legal authority to the government to withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet its expenditure for a financial year, after the Demands for Grants have been voted on by the Lok Sabha. (विनियोग विधेयक — लोकसभा में पारित)

 

• As per the officially released SSC CGL answer key for this question, the Appropriation Bill, 2022 referred to here was passed by the Lok Sabha on May 10, 2022.

 

• Appropriation Bills are Money Bills under Article 110 of the Constitution, and can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, with the Rajya Sabha limited to making non-binding recommendations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4, as per the official answer key.

 

Additional Information

 

• Parliament typically passes more than one Appropriation Bill in a year — the main one after the Budget session, and further ones for supplementary demands for grants passed later in the year.

 

• The Finance Bill, which deals with taxation proposals, is passed separately from the Appropriation Bill.

 

NOTE

 

• March 24, 2022 (Option 1): This is the date most commonly associated with the passage of the main Union Budget's Appropriation Bill for 2022-23, but it is not the option marked correct in the official key for this specific question.

 

• February 20, 2022 (Option 2): Not the date of passage per the official key.

 

• April 20, 2022 (Option 3): Not the date of passage per the official key.

question: What kind of forces arise from transient dipoles in atoms that induce transient dipoles in nearby atoms, produce an attractive force and are significant only over short distances (~500 pm)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is London dispersion forces.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• London dispersion forces (also called instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces) arise due to transient (instantaneous) dipoles created by momentary fluctuations in electron distribution within atoms or non-polar molecules. (लंदन विसरण बल — क्षणिक द्विध्रुव)

 

• These transient dipoles induce corresponding dipoles in neighbouring atoms/molecules, resulting in a weak, short-range attractive force.

 

• These forces are significant only over very short distances (of the order of a few hundred picometres, as mentioned in the question) and weaken rapidly with increasing distance.

 

• London dispersion forces are the weakest type of van der Waals forces but are present in all atoms and molecules, including noble gases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• London dispersion forces are named after physicist Fritz London, who first explained them theoretically using quantum mechanics in 1930.

 

• The strength of London dispersion forces generally increases with increasing molecular size and polarisability.

 

NOTE

 

• Dipole-dipole forces (Option 1): These occur between molecules with permanent dipoles, not transient ones.

 

• Dipole-induced dipole forces (Option 3): These involve a permanent dipole inducing a dipole in a nearby non-polar molecule — different from purely transient dipole-transient dipole interactions.

 

• Hydrogen bond (Option 4): A relatively strong dipole-dipole interaction involving hydrogen bonded to highly electronegative atoms (N, O, F), not transient dipoles.

question: Which of the following combinations of ‘Ruler – Predecessor’ is correct with respect to the Delhi Sultanate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alaudddin Khalji – Jalaluddin Khalji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji founded the Khalji dynasty in 1290 CE, and was succeeded by his nephew and son-in-law, Alauddin Khalji, who assassinated him in 1296 to seize the throne. (अलाउद्दीन खिलजी — जलालुद्दीन खिलजी का उत्तराधिकारी)

 

• This makes 'Alauddin Khalji – Jalaluddin Khalji' (Ruler – Predecessor) the correct combination among the options given.

 

• Alauddin Khalji went on to become one of the most powerful rulers of the Delhi Sultanate, known for his market control reforms and successful campaigns, including against the Mongols.

 

• The other combinations in the options reverse the correct ruler-predecessor relationships of the Khalji and Tughluq dynasties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tughluq dynasty was founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq in 1320, succeeded by his son Muhammad bin Tughluq, who was in turn succeeded by Firuz Shah Tughluq.

 

• The Khalji dynasty ruled from 1290 to 1320, after which the Tughluq dynasty took over the Delhi Sultanate.

 

NOTE

 

• Jalaluddin Khalji – Alauddin Khalji (Option 2): Reverses the actual relationship — Jalaluddin was the predecessor, not the successor, of Alauddin.

 

• Muhammad Tughluq – Firuz Shah Tughluq (Option 3): Reverses the order — Muhammad Tughluq preceded Firuz Shah Tughluq, not the other way around.

 

• Ghiyasuddin Tughluq – Muhammad Tughluq (Option 4): Reverses the order — Ghiyasuddin Tughluq preceded Muhammad Tughluq, not the other way around.

question: For how many days is the Hornbill festival held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hornbill Festival of Nagaland is held annually for 10 days, from 1 to 10 December. (हॉर्नबिल महोत्सव — 10 दिन)

 

• It is organised at the Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near the state capital Kohima, and showcases the cultural heritage of Nagaland's major tribes.

 

• The festival is timed to coincide with Nagaland's Statehood Day (1 December) and is popularly called the 'Festival of Festivals'.

 

• It features traditional dances, crafts, sports, food, and the famous Hornbill International Rock Festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nagaland attained statehood on 1 December 1963, becoming the 16th state of India.

 

• Other cultural festivals of Nagaland include Sekrenyi (Angami tribe) and Moatsu (Ao tribe).

 

NOTE

 

• 5 (Option 1): Incorrect — the festival runs for 10 days, not 5.

 

• 15 (Option 3): Incorrect — the festival does not run for 15 days.

 

• 20 (Option 4): Incorrect — the festival does not run for 20 days.
